# AI Notes

This file documents how AI tools were used while building the Smart Expense Tracker API.

## 1. Which parts of the code were AI-generated vs. written by you

I used Claude and ChatGPT as coding assistants. I owned the main decisions and reviewed the final code.

**Generated by AI**
- Express app setup, middlewares, Joi validators, and Winston logger
- Some APIs were built completely by Claude (filter by category,delete expense, create expense) — routes, controllers, services, and validation. I reviewed them in Postman before keeping them.
- First drafts of tests, Dockerfile, docker-compose, and README

**Written and reviewed by me**
- Overall architecture, stack choices, and API design
- Expense schema/model (`id`, `title`, `amount`, `category`, `date`, collection `expenses`)
- Totals using MongoDB aggregation
- Decision to use MongoDB instead of a JSON file
- This `AI_NOTES.md` file (written by me, polished with AI)

## 2. What you validated, tested, or changed in the AI's output, and why

- I reviewed the APIs Claude built (create, filter, delete) and tested them in Postman to make sure responses and status codes were correct
- I ran `npm test` and checked create, list, filter, totals, and delete until everything worked
- AI first stored data in a JSON file. After concurrent create requests gave wrong results, I changed it to MongoDB with Mongoose and transactions
- I moved totals to MongoDB aggregation so we do not load all expenses into memory just to add them up
- I committed the `.env` file so reviewers can run the project without creating their own env file

## 3. Any AI suggestion you decided not to use, and why

The AI suggested storing expense data in a local JSON file (read the whole file, update it in memory, write it back). I did not accept that approach.

When I tested expense creation with concurrent requests, the results were wrong: multiple expenses ended up with the same title, amount, category, and date even when that was not the intended input set. That came from the JSON file’s read-modify-write pattern, which is not safe under concurrent writes (race conditions / lost updates).

Instead, I insisted on using MongoDB as the database (via Mongoose), with the `expenses` collection in the `SmartExpenseTracker` database, and wrapping create/delete operations in MongoDB transactions so concurrent requests are handled correctly without corrupting or incorrectly duplicating expense data.

I also added concurrency test cases for parallel creates, totals, and deletes; those tests are passing.
